mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened financial conditions and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the month prior to the decision
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 30-day prior period (t-test p > 0.05) during tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls by more than 20 basis points in a month, labor market strength is interpreted as a positive signal for corporate earnings prospects, driving a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by >20 bps in a single month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the 60-day forward return is not statistically superior to the 60-day prior period mean (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in HOUST (household spending index) exceeding 2% in the two months prior to the decision predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals resilient consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >2% month-over-month for two consecutive months before the decision
failure_condition: Across 50 tested episodes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than the 5-day rolling average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 3% for three consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which is expected to depress equity valuations and produce a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥3% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During such supply shocks, the 20-day forward return is not statistically lower than the 30-day prior average (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 4% for three consecutive months, the persistence of low rates is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it reflects accommodative policy and reduced discounting of future earnings.
failure_condition: Over 100 episodes, the 60-day forward return is not statistically higher than the 30-day prior mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in PAYEMS (employment months) by at least 50,000 in a month signals labor market absorption, which is expected to boost earnings expectations and drive a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥50,000 in a single month
failure_condition: In 40 such episodes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 2% in the prior quarter indicate demand weakness, which is expected to depress equity valuations and produce a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls ≥2% and RSAFS falls ≥2% in the prior quarter
failure_condition: Across 30 such dual shocks, the 60-day forward return is not statistically lower than the 30-day prior average (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in CPIAUCSL (CPI) by over 1% in the month preceding the decision, accompanied by a decline in HOUST by at least 1%, signals demand-driven inflation without underlying supply strength, which is expected to produce a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >1% while HOUST decreases by ≥1% in the prior month
failure_condition: In 40 such episodes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.10).
